images.filename: Mitigating data bias and ensuring reliable evaluation of AI models with  shortcut hull learning | Nature Communications
images.img_desc: A three-part scientific schematic explains how shortcut features can bias AI model evaluation and how shortcut hull learning (SHL) addresses the problem. Panel a compares direct learning from datasets with and without shortcuts, showing humans and AI recognizing cats using different features such as the head, body, tail, shape, or texture; the diagram contrasts misleading and reliable assessment results. Panel b illustrates two challenges in diagnosing shortcuts with out-of-distribution data: the exponential growth of possible feature combinations and the difficulty of intervening on features without changing the label. Panel c shows multiple models learning different feature regions and combining them to form a diverse model suite, with annotations about directly learning shortcut hulls and accelerating learning. The graphic uses clean vector illustrations, blue, green, orange, and red accents, labeled arrows, and boxed sections on a white background.
images.caption: Scientific schematic illustrating shortcut-induced bias in AI evaluation and the use of diverse models with shortcut hull learning to obtain more reliable assessments.
images.title: Mitigating data bias and ensuring reliable evaluation of AI models with  shortcut hull learning | Nature Communications
